Far Cry 3 is easily one of Ubisoft's best games and still holds up incredibly well today. 🌴

The Rook Islands are beautiful, atmospheric, and full of things to do. The combination of open-world exploration, gunplay, hunting, crafting, stealth, and outpost liberation makes the gameplay extremely addictive. I especially love how you can approach enemy camps however you want — stealthily, with a sniper rifle, or by simply causing complete chaos.

One of the biggest highlights is definitely Vaas. His character, personality, and unforgettable dialogue make him one of the best villains in gaming. Michael Mando's performance is absolutely fantastic. It's a shame that the story doesn't maintain quite the same level after Vaas.

Despite being an older game, the graphics and atmosphere still look great. The tropical environment, wildlife, soundtrack, and exploration make the world feel alive.

Overall, Far Cry 3 is a must-play for anyone who enjoys open-world FPS games. It's one of those games that helped define the modern open-world formula and remains one of Ubisoft's classics.

[h1]Price (regular): $29.99 ($39.99 for deluxe)[/h1]

[h1]Price (lowest): $7.49 (75% off)[/h1]

[h1]My overall rating: 9.5/10[/h1]
Easily one of my favorite games of all time.

[h1]Value: 9/10[/h1]
Most other games this age are already down to $20, however the singleplayer is a lot longer than most other action/shooter games, making it well worth the price.

[h1]Singleplayer: 10/10[/h1]
Amazing singleplayer. Capturing outposts is probably the best part. There are over 30 spread over the massive map. The main story has some pretty good action too. Plus there is hunting, racing, and assassination side missions and a lot of other things that are a lot of fun.

[h1]Co-op: 5/10 (2-4 players)[/h1]
Co-op has some serious issues. When the match tries to launch it almost always crashes or freezes when loading. Due to this you wont be able to find players unless you are playing with friends. When it works it is decent but doesnt have the openness that makes far cry great. Update: co-op has been working better lately.

[h1]Multiplayer: 6.5/10[/h1]
The multiplayer is actually pretty good, but a little generic. Doesn't have enough players to reach its full potential though.

[h1]Content: 9.5/10[/h1]
Both the co-op and multiplayer are pretty basic, but the singleplayer makes up for it. You of course have the story and outposts, but there is also tons of ruins and caves to be explored for relics and loot, side missions, trials, races, dlc missions, and even knife throwing and poker.

[h1]Length: 10/10[/h1]
An average playthrough of the singleplayer will take you roughly 30 hours, doing the main storyline capturing all the outposts and doing most of the side missions.

[h1]Story: 8/10[/h1]
The story really tries to be great and in some ways it is but also is a little flat. You and your friends are having the time of your life until getting caught by slavers on a remote island. You escape and have to save your friends and liberate the natives from the pirates in the process.

[h1]Gameplay: 10/10[/h1]
Very good, open gameplay. Most situations you can choose to attack however you like. Climb any mountain for a good vantage point with a sniper rifle, use stealth with a bow and using knife takedowns, attack head on with an lmg, or charge in with a truck with c4 planted on it.

[h1]With freinds: 6/10[/h1]
The co-op and multiplayer are pretty fun with friends but doesnt have a lot of substance.

[h1]Graphics: 9/10[/h1]
Good graphics, very good considering the scale of the game.

[h1]Physics: 9.5/10[/h1]
Maybe not as smooth walking around a small area and shooting a few people as call of duty, but all in all the physics are a lot better than just about any other game. Driving really feels good. Good fire physics, you can light large areas of brush with a flamethrower.

[h1]Performance: 9/10[/h1]
Works good for the most part. Can easily play it on max setting with my laptop, core i7 4810mq @ 2.80 GHz (turbo to 3.80 GHz) 12gbs ram and gtx870m 3gbs dedicated. Haven't had any notable issues or bugs.

[h1]Sound: 8/10[/h1]
Sound is good but maybe a little rough here and there.

[h1]Polished: 8/10[/h1]
Nothing majorly wrong with it but it does have the usual trees growing through rocks and animals spawning inside stuff.

[h1]Atmosphere: 8.5/10[/h1]
The vast landscape gives you a good immersive feel but could be better if they didn't have so much of the same plants making it all feel the same.

[h1]Objectives: 7/10[/h1]
Objectives are pretty basic. Pretty much go fight through these people and do (insert objective here). Some are a little more in depth.

[h1]Clarity: 9/10[/h1]
No problems with knowing where to go or what to do. The story line is linear and very easy to follow.

[h1]World: 9.5/10[/h1]
Unparalleled world. Massive world with large mountains, caves, ruins, shanty towns, vast foliage, ocean, and tons of wildlife to try and kill you. Although most of the landscape has the same trees and plants so a lot of it looks the same.

[h1]Characters: 8/10[/h1]
The characters are interesting. The antagonists really make you want to kill them. All the characters are just a little thin but still good.

[h1]UI: 6.5/10[/h1]
The menus are pretty poor. Pulling up your map is really slow. All other menus are in the escape menu which is pretty slow and not that great to navigate. Plus there's Uplay which is horrible.

[h1]Controls: 9/10[/h1]
Mostly standard controls. Not my favorite layout but close enough I didn't feel the need to change anything.

[h1]Freedom: 10/10[/h1]
As much freedom as you could ask for. You can ignor your current mission to go off capturing outpost, doing side mission, or just go for a nature hike.

[h1]Influence: 2.5/10[/h1]
The story itself is very linear. Only choice in the game is the ending and what happens after.

[h1]Settings: 9/10[/h1]
Four difficulty setting so good for most any skill level. Average control options.

[h1]Character progression: 6/10[/h1]
Sometimes feels like they resticked what you can do at the beginning instead of allowing you to do more later on.

[h1]Weapon selection: 9/10[/h1]
Has plenty of weapons. Handguns, SMGs, assault rifles, shotguns, LMGs, sniper rifles, launchers, explosives, and specials. Over 30 total, though some feel similar.

[h1]Customization: 7/10[/h1]
Most weapons can be modded. Higher level guns can have up to 3 mods. Mods incude extended mags, silencers, and several types of sights, though most guns are limited on which mods are available. Almost all weapons can be painted.

[h1]AI: 8.5/10[/h1]
For the most part the ai is fairly intelegent. Considering what they have to do in an open world unrelated to a story, it's very good. Though this causes a few quirks.

[h1]Up to date: 9/10[/h1]
Only came out at the end of 2012 and there isn't any notable aging to the game. Not lacking anything that newer games might have.

[h1]Replayability: 8.5/10[/h1]
The story doesnt give incentive replay it, but since you can whatever you like however you like, the rest of the game has a lot of replay value.

[h1]Pace: 8.5/10[/h1]
For such a long game the balance between length and action is very good. You can go straight to the next mission, rush through a few outposts, or take your time doing everything at your own pace.

[h1]Repetitiveness: 8/10[/h1]
If you were to just walk up with an assault rifle everytime it would probably get very repetitive, but change up your approach everytime and it won't be much at all.

[h1]Realism: 8.5/10[/h1]
It has some good aspects and a few poor ones when it comes to how realistic it is. Even compared to other games the amount of people you are able to kill is a little ridiculous. It has some supernatural elements which isn't bad but they are a little lame and seem to be inspired by acid trips. Other than that it's actually got good physics and overall better than most games.

[h1]DLC: 5/10[/h1]
The downloadable content is all pretty mediocre. A few independent short story missions that are okay, some co-op and multiplayer content, and a few other things that are all insignificant.

[h1]Achievements: 6/10[/h1]
50 achievements but only on Uplay not Steam, and 6 are for co-op making them near impossible. The rest of the achievements are great. Good amount and some challenging but nothing too hard.

[h1]Trading cards: N/A[/h1]
Doesn't have Steam badges/trading cards.

[h1]Series improvement: 10/10[/h1]
Far Cry 2 was a good game, however has aged a lot and lacked in a few aspects. Far Cry 3 did a great job at improving and made a very well rounded, good performing game.

[h1]Originality: 10/10[/h1]
Bottom line is that no other game is very much like Far Cry. Maybe slightly similar to games like Just Cause or some RPGs and it may have some Tomb Raider elements but not enough that its overall gameplay is at all the same as anything else.

I see comparisons to Skyrim and Witcher 3 thrown out there, and I assure you, those comparisons are entirely inaccurate. Content-wise, this game has a fraction of the content. Story-wise, even less. I enjoy this game, but comparing it to Skyrim or Witcher 3 is completely baseless. The comparisons to Skyrim were just people repeating the marketing for the game, and the comparison to The Witcher 3 were just people deciding "oh, well if it's like Skyrim, then it's also like The Witcher 3." It's nothing like either of those.

While this is certainly a good game, the gameplay does become repetitive pretty fast, with the majority of gameplay time being repeating the same task of taking over one camp after another after another, and the camps aren't a whole lot different from eachother. There's a lot of elements common to other open world games, like racing challenges and such, to help break the monotony of taking over another camp.

The main issue I have with the story (or lack of story) is that the protagonist is pretty unlikeable: a privileged rich 20-something tourists. Oblivious, he selects an island chain in the middle of a guerilla war revolution as the destination for his Jet-Ski / Skydiving tropical holiday with his rich early 20's friends. Their lack of awareness results in death and kidnapping, and it's up to the protagonist not only to rescue his remaining friends who haven't died due to their own cluelessness, but he must enter the war as a savior of these downtrodden people who, despite being *ridiculously* well armed, need him to step in to single-handedly fight their war for them, because obviously they can't do it themselves. They need the rich 20 year old kid who stumbled onto their conflict as a good spot for a high price adventure vacation to save the day, because obviously this guy's got his sh.t together. The story very much smacks of Edgar Rice Burroughs, or possibly is a page torn directly out of his work. The whole thing feels very much like something he'd write today.

[h2]Far Cry 3 Review[/h2]

Far Cry 3 is an open-world shooter with light RPG mechanics released by Ubisoft in the year 2012 and quickly became a modern classic. The things that made this game a dear among gamers are: On one side, how well it mixes the gameplay elements of a sandbox with a meaningful and fun progression system. On the other side how great the characters and the story is. Yes, I’m talking about Vaas, but not exclusively.

In Far Cry 3 you play as Jason Brody, a spoiled rich kid, that has to save his kidnapped friends from a band of pirates and slavers led by Vaas Montenegro and his boss Hoyt Volker. TLDR you are free to kill, hunt, loot and steal to your heart’s content.

[h1] Questions you might have if you're interested in playing it: [/h1]

[list]
[*][b]What is it exactly that you do in the game?[/b]

You explore the fictional archipelago of Rook Islands, you shoot everything that moves and loot everything that doesn’t. There are elements of tomb raiding and light roleplaying in the game, but the core of the game is having fun shooting stuff.

[*][b] Will it make my eyes bleed?[/b]

I don’t think so. For a game of 2012 it looks surprisingly good. Yes, some characters have weird uncanny eyes and some animals look like they had been oiled and stuffed with glue, but the environment still looks great. Overall it's a little bit dated but not too bad.

[*][b]Does it have a good story?[/b]

To put it simple: Yes! I’m amazed at how relevant it still is. Without giving away too much, it’s a story about madness, violence and how power corrupts everything. It’s thought provoking and fun at the same time.

[*][b]Does it have a good soundtrack?[/b]

It enhances the experience of the game: I won’t call it “mind-blowing”, but it never gets in the way of the story or the game plan and gets the job done. It’s OK.

[*][b]Does it have replay value?[/b]

Gameplay-wise: yes. You have a huge selection of guns to use at your disposal and with how dynamic the game world is you will be engaged for hours.
Story-wise: not so much, the game only has a few endings and they are functionally the same. I had tons of fun with the characters and the lore of the game, but once you complete it, you won’t get much out of it (unless you are into fan theories).

[*][b]Does it run well?[/b]

Yes, it has some minor bugs and glitches, but nothing game breaking. I can tell you from my own experience that this game doesn’t run well on 2012 hardware. Keep that in mind.

[*][b]Is it fun?[/b]

Hell yes! It’s a blast. Almost everything that you do in the game is fun and rewarding.
[/list]


[h1] So, why is Far Cry 3 still relevant?[/h1]

Like most open world games, you start being almost useless at everything and with the power of violence and friendship, you climb your way through the food chain to become the apex hunter. What makes Far Cry 3 great is how well doing some things in it feels. Shooting feels snappy and responsive, and with the huge quantity of guns to buy or unlock, you always have a gun worth trying or upgrading. Exploring is rewarding, everything that you discover, loot or steal will give you a new gun, exp or money to spend on new equipment. Hell, even climbing towers, an Ubisoft standard, not only unlocks that section of the map for you, but also awards you with those things. It’s amazing.


[h1] Things that I like about this game:[/h1]
[list]
[*]Exploring is rewarding and engaging. There is always something fun to do, some animal or person to hunt and some special item to grind or loot.

[*]It has a story like no other and every secondary character is interesting.

[*]It’s a game that respects your time. Everything has a worthy reward associated with it.

[*]Most of the side content is fun.

[*]The game world is huge and immersive, it feels alive.
[/list]

[h1] Things that I dislike about this game:[/h1]

[list]
[*]Some animations could be shorter, like getting in a car. I get that they want to try to make you feel wrapped in their world, but sometimes the game goes to the extreme with the animations.

[*]The hitboxes for looting corpses are finicky.

[*]This game really loves to flash you with white screens. Only during some main missions’ cinematics, but is still annoying.

	
[/list]

[h1] Is this game worth my hard earned money?[/h1]

This game is a blast. I’m surprised at how well it feels and how fun it is. Yes, sure, some missions are annoying and sometimes you will randomly die because the game RNG throws everything at you. But the story is compelling, the gameplay is fun and the characters in it are entertaining.

[h1]The Story[/h1]
You are Jason Brody, partying with your friends and family to celebrate your little brother attaining his pilot's license.
However, things aren't going to be all fun and games as you are kidnapped by pirates and will be seeing death before finally escaping their claws.
You happen to be saved by the natives of the island, the Rakyat, and for them to help you rescue your friends, you have to do them a favor, too. Consequently, you leave the face of the rich kid behind and set out to become a savior, a warrior, and an avenger.
If this setting didn't sound like it could be fun for you, let me tell you that this game shines through its storytelling - sadly saying anything more would be a spoiler.
Additionally, don't fret about buying a short game - completing the story with all it has to offer, may take up to a good 40h.
 
[h1]The World[/h1]
As the destination of this little vacation, you chose a tropical island, somewhere in the middle of the sea.
The island offers you a great variety of wildlife, that you can choose to hunt - but be wary that some of these animals prefer to be the hunter instead of the hunted.
Moreover, the geography is just great - there is a lot of vertical movement that can be done and if you are lucky you will find some kind of glider atop a hill and be equipped to fly miles across the island.
 
[h1]The Characters[/h1]
[olist]
[*] Jason Brody - there isn't much known regarding the background of the protagonist, however from the little intro sequence and the appearance of his family it looks like he grew up well hidden from the wicked of the globe, with nothing to care about in the world.
[*] Friends and Family - your little and big brother, girlfriend and some more sidekicks. Saying that, I intend it the way it sounds like, you never really get to know a lot about the relationship between you and all the others, which left me not really caring about them.
[*] Dennis - he is one of the Rakyat, your savior and the one who could see the warrior in you, he seems like a chill guy, and his tattoo drawing skills are top notch.
[*] Citra - the leader of the tribe, she is a special woman but has only her and her tribe’s best in mind. She wants power more than anything.
[*] Thats not to say that every character in the game is bad or weak. There are interesting and fun  ones, however, I can't mention them here without spoiling the fun. Let's just say, some will speak a little german...
[*] Vaas - this is the one you have been anticipating. If a game makes you care more about the villain than any other character - it did something damn right. Vaas is absolutely motherfucking crazy - and you will love it.
[/olist]
 
[h1]The Gameplay[/h1]
It's a first person shooter, nothing special in that regard. 
However, the stealth aspect with its melee takedowns is so satisfying and combined with your environment and all the things to do and sites to go to the gameplay really shines.
Throughout the island, there are communication towers scattered, which you can climb to extend the map and gain access to new weapons.
Speaking of weapons - [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p764p7GbX78]the variety is great[/url] and you can even customize them with skins, which has a cool feel to it.
Other than that the pirates have set up camp in various places around the island and you can conquer them guns blazing or eliminate every single person without them knowing what hit them.
The latter will give you, aside from your feeling of accomplishment, bonus [i]experience[/i] and won't trigger the alarm for enemy reinforcement.
Should you have been surprised at the word "experience" - yes, there is a skill tree which grants you cool new abilities - like being able to take down multiple enemies from above or under water.
Last but not least you can also craft various items, most importantly syringes used for health recovery in combat.
 
[h1]The Visuals[/h1]
The game is powered by the [i]Dunia Engine[/i], if this doesn't ring a bell, saying it's a derivative of the [i]CryEngine[/i] should.
That being said - the game looks incredible. Let alone the setting on a tropical island, the deep, dense jungle, extending into bright beaches and ending into the crystal clear, blue ocean.
Perhaps sun reflected on the water is just one of my personal obsessions, but it looks just so incredible.
 
[h1]The Sound[/h1]
It's really good - you hear pirates screaming around the island; yourself mumbling things, which really enhance the feeling of character progression and the wildlife around in the jungle sounds amazingly terrifying.
Weapon sounds seem good; moving through high grass and leaves appears realistic and cutting into flesh is pleasing, to say the least.
[spoiler]Ultimately, let me just say this - burning down fields of weed with a flamethrower to dubstep powered by [i]Skrillex[/i] is definitely memorable.[/spoiler]
 
[h1]The Verdict[/h1]
Do yourself a favor and try this game, it doesn't matter if you are not a fan of first person shooters, or if the story doesn't call home to you at first.

Far Cry 3 is one of those open-world games that actually makes you FEEL you'd WANT to explore the Rook Islands with its varied wild flora AND fauna (hostile or indifferent), as well as the various enemies (pirates or privateers) and with the Rakyat assisting at times. The story missions are quite a lot of fun, and if you level up properly none of them are very difficult (i.e. do the stealth kills and try to take down outposts undetected to get extra XP for the skills). 

You started out as a party guy Jason Brody, who can't do anything. Your brother Grant was the ex-Army, and somehow you ended up captured on this island held by pirates and right in the INTRO sequence your brother got killed and your mad dash to freedom ended up with you diving over a waterfall, but you lived, and you woke up in a village, and handed your first mission... and a wimply pistol... get up this tower on top of the hill, and activate it. 

From there on, you steadily progress from a wimpy adrenaline junky to a fearsome killing machine capable of mowing down squads of professional mercenaries with LMG or assault rifle, hit wings off a fly at 100 yards with a sniper rifle, blade dance with professional knife fighters, stealth kill like a ninja, as you liberate the Rook Islands from two megalomaniacs, Vaas, and his boss, Hoyt, while recovering your friends one by one. 

The islands are beautiful, and the animals behave independently of you. Goats and Buffalos and pigs and more wander the landscape, and predators like bears, leopards, even tigers wander the wild hunting them, and if you get in the way, you as well. In the ocean there are bull sharks and regular fish, and in the swamps there are crocodiles. Yes, it's a ton of fun exploring the place. There are small villages, pirate and merc outposts (that you can liberate... by killing everybody), unoccupied villages that were sites of atrocities, more radio towers you can deactivate, plus for the obssessive collectors, various artifacts to collect, such as 120 relics from the past cultures (including one from Chinese history!) letters from the Japanese WW2 occupation (plenty of bodies left around), memory cards left in outposts detailing the sordid narc industry links of Rook Island, as well as different animals and plants (they go in the survival handbook). 

There are also untold number of caves, underground passages, leading to totally unknown areas deep within the bowels of the island that makes you wonder if you're playing Tomb Raider. :D  Indeed, the radio towers and many other sequences do require a bit of jumping and climbing to accomplish. 

Even on the surface, there are random things happening. Friendly and enemy jeeps patrol the routes. Enemy soldiers will patrol, and sometimes, force march prisoners / slaves on the road. You may engage, or not as you see fit, but they are excellent source of XPs, as valid as any one. And animals do roam the island, as it is wild out there. 

There are plenty of side missions, some of which are handed out by locals, like "help find my daughter, who ran away with boyfriend!"  in addition to the story missions. Furthermore, conquered outposts often have bounty missions (kill a pirate or a merc and his minions) as well as "path of the hunter" missions (hunt down X animals using provided weapons). (HINT: you only have to use the same CLASS of weapon, not the specific weapon. If they provide a regular .45ACP, bring your customized .44 Magnum or .50AE Desert Eagle)

Ah, speaking of weapons... lots and lots of weapons. Pistols, sniper rifles, shotguns, assault rifiles, grenade launchers, light machine guns, special weapons (including recurve bow), and signature weapons. Some weapons can be customized with different type of sights, extended magazines, even a suppressor. And there are different paintjobs available too. Add the oddballs, like repair tool (welding torch), flamethrower, and even a flare gun... and things can get interesting indeed. Did I mention that many vehicles have mounted weapons, like a HMG that you can wield?  

How you tackle mission (usually involving killing everybody at a certain place) is entirely up to you. Run and gun? Snipe and hide? Silent and deadly? Lure and ambush? It is all up to you. When you have the best sniper rifle (.50 cal with suppressor two-stage zoom scope) you can kill even a heavy with a single shot to the head from afar. There are also sometimes captured predators that you can "liberate" with a shot to the cage, thus letting it attack the enemies in the camp for you! Remember, bonus points if you were never detected (1500 xp instead of 500 xp). 

I have tried many open-world games before, from Far Cry 2 to Mercenaries 2, from GTA 3 (and sequels) to many others. Far Cry 3 stands above the rest because it is so well balanced. it doesn't unlock too many skills (some require you to unlock via story missions) at once, no matter how much XP you accumulated. it also doesn't unlock the 2nd island until well past 75% point. At each point you are reminded of the stakes you're playing with... the lives of your friends that may still be in pirate's hands, and each and every one will be scarred for life. The villians are psychopaths, but interesting psychopaths. And the other characters that you meet? They all have their own motivations, which may or may not match your own. 

Somehow, FC3 just struck the right balance between too "scattered brained", i.e. "Too many choices! What do I do now?" vs. "where's the freedom? I am bored, I want to do something ELSE"...  And there are plenty of variety in the missions as well as outposts. On the hunt missions, you have to use the specified weapon class/type., which can be challenging, such as hunting tigers with a pistol, or bears with a shotgun. On the bounty missions, you are to kill the one or two "leaders" with your blade. The rest are up to you with no restrictions. Just keep in mind in late game there can be two leaders with a dozen minions around them, and killing them all can be a difficult endeavor, esp. if you can only knife the leaders. 

The skills you learn are divided into three categories: crane, shark, and spider, which of which has a different "tree". As mentioned before, they are unlocked by progressing in the story missions and can be learned by spending "skill points" which are earned by every few thousand XP. And they add a lot of fun abilities, such as chain takedowns, knife throw take down, grenade takedown, double take down, death from above, death from below, and so on. 

There are bazillion crates scattered on the island, each containing some artifacts and/or money. You can further loot the bodies (enemy or friendly) for more artifacts, many of which can be sold for $$$. If you have killed some fauna, you cna often skin them for making containers / slings for ammo, wallet, and so on, and it's the only way you can carry more weapons, more ammo, even more money. In fact, you can also craft herbal medicine from the plants you gathered (which are generically divided into "colored leaves", and you need X of Red and Y of yellow and so on. As you progress you'll learn other formulas, like animal repellant, hunting instinct (lets you see animals, even behind hills), as well as herbal medicine that just heals you, deep dive potion that lets you go below 60 meters deep, and more. 

All in all, Far Cry 3 is a ton of fun with variety of missions, side mission, as well as plenty of freeform encounter play. The story of growth and one man's journey from wimp to hero is the story of the player. And THAT ultimately, is why it's so much fun.

[h1]Exceptional open-world shooter with a dark twist[/h1]

[i]Far Cry 3[/i] was developed by Ubisoft Montréal & Shanghai and published late 2012 to great ciritcal acclaim. I played it only recently (early 2015), but even though some years old, this game feels like it was made recently. As the third installment in the famous [i]Far Cry[/i] franchise, it continues upon the open-world orientated gameplay establised by [i]Far Cry 2[/i], while fixing almost all of the problems that game had and offering a feel and way of playing all of its own.

The game makes one identify to a degree with Jason Brody, the playable protagonist who is taken captive together with his friends on a tropical island by a gang of pirates lead by someone called Vaas. The opening sequence of the game, from the initial cutscene with the rather vainly partying friends up to the first encounter with Vaas and the escape from his claws, stands out as a classic way of making clear what a game is all about. Vaas is a sinister character, as dark and evil as one could imagine, and more. His fascination with utter violence and the madness of the human mind offers some memorable gaming moments, that made me stare at my screen in utter disbelief and will stay with me for a long time.
Jason Brody starts out as a rather unsure would-be-hero, who is shocked whenever he sees someone killed, and who is very reluctant to kill himself. But his encounter with the sheer evil of Vaas and his fellow criminals, gradually turns him into a killing machine, with only one goal: to free his friends, and ultimately seek revenge. The game cleverly underscores this development by offering some role-playing element: finishing missions or killing enemies grants experience points and levels you up so that you can acquire several abilities which help to overcome obstacles more easily. While the game is rather challenging during its first hours, with raising in level and acquiting more special abilities and better weapons it gets easier, which helps to get the idea of turning into a mean killing machine rather well.

Apart from Jason Brody and Vaas, [i]Far Cry 3[/i] contains several interesting and even unique characters along with three "factions" spread out on two distinct islands. There are too many characters to mention them all, but standing out apart from Vaas is Citra, the priestess of the natives who introduces an almost palpable sexual, brooding tension into the game. One of the best parts of the game is the excellent voice-acting: every charachter, how odd or sinister, is made completely believable through his or her voice.
The world itself is huge: longer journeys can take up to ten minutes, even by car, jeep or boat (of which there are several types). All in all, the story is not only gripping and very well told, it is combined with the freedom of an open world in a very convincing way. You can play this game in several different ways, the options being almost limitless. Following the main story is a valid possibility, but I found it more interesting to divert from this quite often, roaming around in the astoundingly beautiful world in order to capture an enemy outpost (either by force, stealth or cunning, the choice is once more yours!), gather some useful plants or just hunt for animals (who offer several rewards as well).
Apart from the 38 missions in the main storyline, there are over two hundred (!!) side-missions, ranging from stealth kills to hunting specific animals with a specific weapon, trying one's driving skills in a race, climbing communication towers in order to reveal parts of the map or even playing some poker. The amount of gaming hours to be got in singleplayer alone runs into several dozens or more, comparable to a game in that other famous open-world franchise, [i]Assassin's Creed[/i]. I tried the multiplayer as well, but the servers are almost empty by now, alone the rather bland co-op still offers some possibilities.

Apart from the amazing game- and gunplay, the game is a prime example of state-of-the-art graphics and sound, excellently optimized and hardly showing that it was primarily aimed at consoles. It runs flawlessly on my 7-year old pc with a 2,66 Ghz cpu, 4 GB ram and a GeForce GTX 650 ti. All the expected options and tweaks for optimal performance are there, but it has to be said: the game does look much better on the highest settings (very high or ultra), so even if it costs you some fps, do try those. The one thing that could offset several players is the mandatory use of the "infamous" Uplay, a platform that gets huge criticism more often than not. However, for me Uplay just works fine, not only in this but in every other game I played on it. Granted, the achievements are a bit pointless since they don't show on Steam, but the possibility of unlocking extra content by gaining U-points in quite nice. Apart from that, the few dlc packets for the game are completely superfluous, but that's a very, very minor criticism.

Anyone interested in the recent developments of first-person shooters or in the way a modern game can tell a story in combination with an open gaming world, should buy and play this game.

After finishing this game for the 6th time, I can safely say it is still an absolute masterpiece. I’ve played through it 5 or 6 times in total since 2013, but all of those runs were back on the standalone Uplay launcher. Coming back to it on Steam after an 8 year break, I was really excited to hunt all the achievements from scratch. Unfortunately, the Ubisoft launcher automatically synced my old data on the first boot and instantly unlocked every single achievement. It was a massive bummer because I genuinely wanted the satisfaction of earning them again.

Despite that frustrating launcher issue, the game itself holds up beautifully. The stealth sandbox and core gameplay are just so incredibly fun. Visually, I honestly think it looks much better than Far Cry 4, the tropical island aesthetic and summer vibes give it a beautiful, vibrant look that the sequel lacked. The landscapes, ancient temples, and hidden WWII ruins, bunkers, rusted tanks and planes make exploring the world incredibly immersive. The story is fantastic too, and the final choice actually feels impactful, unlike the disappointing "choose A or choose A" illusion of choice you get in the fourth game. Plus, playing through this story again reminds you why Vaas is one of the best villains ever written. Honestly, replaying this game six times might actually be the literal definition of insanity, but I regret nothing, especially when the soundtrack is this brilliant. There is still nothing quite like the absolute chaotic joy of burning down weed fields with a flamethrower while Skrillex and Damian Marley blast in the background.

If I have one real complaint about the mechanics, it’s the parkour. For a 2012 game made by Ubisoft - the literal creators of Assassin's Creed, the climbing and movement feel surprisingly clunky and poorly executed. You can really feel the contrast when you look at a studio like Techland; they were way less popular back then, but they absolutely nailed first-person movement just two and a half years later in Dying Light (even if their stealth wasn't nearly as good as Far Cry's).

At the end of the day, clunky parkour and broken achievement syncs can't ruin what is fundamentally a phenomenal game. Six playthroughs later, and it's still an amazing experience. Highly recommended!

If I remember correctly Far Cry 3 was launched during a time when Ubisoft publicly hated PC Gaming community altogether (pirates…remember?)! And I’m glad they never abandoned the platform despite moving off Steam in 2019. 
It’s a bit ironic considering this was the ultimate gaming experience anyone with a high-end system could ask for back in 2012. Ubisoft didn’t shy away from pushing level of detail up-to that point. Sure, it’s not Crysis 2 but it comes close (in terms of visuals and sound). 

[h1]Pros[/h1]
+Despite loving the overall game, I felt like the story was complete non-sense and bs.
+Built on Crytek's groundbreaking Dunia game engine; Upgraded enough with fine optimization, more colorful environment and high res textures. One of few 7th gen game's not held down by consoles. If you've seen FC3 gameplay at 4K yoou know what I'm talking about.
+Nearly flawless non-linear FPS gameplay. Excellent shooting and cover mechanics.
+Good enemy A.I
+Dense open world full of places to explore and a wide range of wildlife to hunt.
+The campaign sets you through jungles, beaches, underground caves, ancient temples, hidden tombs full of secrets and treasures. 
+There's always something else to do if you're bored of the main story!
+Insane amount of detail and polygon count (play at 4K if you want to see what I'm saying).
+DirectX 11 features. Excellent anti-aliasing methods in-game. 
+Voice acting and motion capture work for the main cast was done well.
+loading screens are short (none when traversing around the island(s). They're a bit long when you fast travel or load the saved game.
+Amazing fire simulation.
+Easy to complete Uplay achievements, bonus Ubi Club rewards like game soundtrack and extra missions. 
+Fully voiced main character.

[h1]Cons[/h1]
-Auto-save system is really weird…auto-saves only work when you buy a new gear or once you complete a mission. Hunting an animal, picking up items, treasures, will NOT save your progress. You could essentially loose hours worth of progress unknowingly.
-Story and narrative pacing often felt forced and dull. 
-Super-natural elements should have been kept minimal at best. 
-Side missions are pretty lame fetch quests. Ubisoft had so much potential to use Rook Island as a means for to tell more stories or lore or just anything interesting.  
-Way too many collectibles and treasures to collect. This is perhaps the biggest flaw with nearly Every Ubisoft game since 2007’s first Assassin’s Creed. 100% completion is a chore and takes away the fun. 
-No Steam Achievements, trading cards :(
-Driving felt a bit clunky. The devs should have opted for third person camera as an option for driving. Nevertheless, it forced you to explore the dense island on-foot and that's isn't the worst thing!
-The Rakyat (essentially the good guys in Blues, the cult that worships the ancient Gods or something like that) become quite annoying after a while. They often repeat the same 3 lines of dialogue....
-Dead multiplayer
-Barebones, linear and repetitive 4 player co-op maps.
-Steam version requires Uplay launcher at all times.

[h1] Some Tips [/h1]
1] Once you're done with basic tutorial you’re free to explore the island so take it as an advantage. Avoid completing too many story missions early on. Just keep hunting!! Go and hunt deer, goats, and boars in order to expand your loot carrying capacity and ability to hold weapons. Just don't forget hunting....
2] Save often. Don't rely on auto-save…
3] Avoid buying guns, ammo or body armour; Seriously money is already scarce and the last thing you would want is having upgrades. You can get nearly every gun for by just liberating an towers (takes around 5 minutes max to do that and additionally you also gain tons of XPs). Ammo can be found in loot crates (there are at least 1000 of them scattered everywhere xD)
4] Clear every Outpost for maxing out Jason's Rakyat tattoo asap and if possible and find every letter and memory card. 

[h1]FINAL THOUGHTS[/h1]
Far Cry 3 is one of the finest Ubisoft games, everything feels fresh, organic and actually fun to play! If you're looking for an open world adventure game Far Cry 3 is the perfect entry to start. Get it for on sale without thinking twice. Worth $20 listing price considering the amount of content you get! A lot of gamers would agree that this is the best game in the series 8 years after it's release in 2020.

[h1]How I Found Out About "Far Cry 3"[/h1]
Well, where to start. To put it simply, I rented Far Cry 3 on the Ps3 a little while after it came out. After it's release, weeks went by, as I heard more and more about Far Cry 3. Nothing was spoiled, but I heard so many good things about it. At the time, I really didn't have the money, so I decided to rent the game, like I use to do back in the day.

After picking up the game, I was able to play through about half of it, before needing to take it back. However, around Christmas, my parents got me Far Cry 3 on the Ps3 and I was able to finish my adventure.

About six months after that, I saw the Deluxe Edition of Far Cry 3 on sale on Steam, and picked it up. Then things became really good. 

[h1]Unfair FIrst Impressions[/h1]
Every game genre gets hate by some people. Mainly because of opinions, which is okay. There are genre' I don't like, and others I do. However, the main thing I see about Far Cry 3 in reviews that give it a low score is.....Uplay. Why, oh why must you give the [b]GAME[/b] a bad score because it uses Uplay? I understand, it's annyoing at times, especially needing to run it through two different clients, but to give the game itself a bad score because it uses Uplay, is very unfair. I have never had any problems running Far Cry 3 through both Steam & Uplay. Basically, when it says someone is playing Far Cry 3 on Steam, they actually have their Uplay open, as the game itself doesn't need to be running to say you're actually in-game.

Not to mention, Far Cry 3 has crafting in it, along with survival tactics. Someone went as far to report the game for being a Minecraft clone because of it. 

[h1]Review Of "Far Cry 3"[/h1]
Far Cry 3 is an [b]open world[/b], [b]first person shooter[/b], [b]survival type[/b] game. With a very in depth story. Good and memorable characters. Amazing world, and game mechanics. 

The game takes you in the shoes of "Jason Brody", a rich kid who takes a vaction to an island with a group of friends. Before having enough time to enjoy themselves, Jason and his friends find themselves captured by pirates ruled by "Vass". It's Jason's job to break out of the slave camp and get his friends back. Having never shot or killed anyone, it is up to you to learn how to take down your foe using a wide variety of weapons. Using drugs made off of plants from the jungle, and working alongside people like Denis. Can you make it happen?

Far Cry 3 allows you to form your story. Everyone's playthrough will be different. 

The world of Far Cry 3. The world is massive. In my Just Cause 2 review, I talked about the world being massive, but mostly empty. Here, the world is not only massive, it isn't empty. Everywhere there is something to collect, capture, destroy, hide from, or [b]DIE[/b] from. The world is split between two islands, which take part at different sections of the story. Each lush with plains, jungle's , a lot of killer animals, green, some more green, beautiful oceans and caves. Far Cry 3 is a graphically intense looking game. The views are just amazing. The world is populated by loot, like weapons, money, and relics. There are also deadly animals, like the Tiger, or Cassowary. Not only that, pirates, who only mean to kill you. 

Far Cry 3 does it nicely, where the whole game isn't out to kill you. The pirates will get into fights with the natives. Angry animals will attack civilians, and pirates. You could sit at a far, watching through the scope of a sniper rifle, as a Tiger slips through the enemy defense and takes down a group. 

Thrown about this world are these plants. These plants can be used to craft drugs to help you with many things. Like detecting animals, or increasing maximum health, etc. Along with crafting drugs, you can also craft other items. Like wallets to carry more money, weapon holsters to carry more weapons, or munitions pouch to carry more grenades. One thing that's strange about this is the fact that you must skin animals to craft these. However, for one thing you might need 2 Tiger skin, and the next, 1 Deer skin, see my problem with this?

Scatered around the world are [b]strongholds[/b] or "outposts" that are controlled by the pirates. You can take these down by killing all pirates on the inside. By capturing one of these strongholds, it makes the territory around you safe, and creates a fast travel system. Now, how you approach these strongholds to take them down is all up to you. You have full freedom to do what you want. You could run right in with heavy machine guns blazing it out. You sit from a far with a sniper rifle and pick them off. You could sneak in, perform takedowns and use a stealth recurve bow. Or you could lure an animal into the base. There are so many things you could do. 

To take down these strongholds, you need weapons, right? Worry no more. The weapons provided in Far Cry 3 consist of pistols, SMG's, Assault rifles, snipers, shotguns, HMG's, flare gun's, flame throwers, and way more.

Now, while on a mission, though they provide a good story, you are restricted most of the time. Meaning you can't really approach the way you may want to. 

Alongside the main story, you of course have side missions. These are of two types, but work and are fun. The first of them being the Hunter missions. Where you take out an animal for various reasons. The second being the Wanted Dead missions, where it is your job to take down a baddie with your knife/machete. 

You also earn XP for getting kills and completing missions. XP will gain you skill points, which then lead to you choosing a skill you'd like. One problem with this system is, you don't have access to all the skills until you get futher into the story. As the skills move on, they get kind of more useless. However that's just my opinion.

If there is really anything else I don't care about in this game, it's that the second half falls short of the first half. It doesn't really keep the hype going, it kind of dies down. 

[h1]Thoughts (Other)[/h1]
I'd like to post this here. Far Cry 3 is so far my most favorite single player experience of all time. The story was great, the gameplay was great. The soundtrack is amazing, and brings man tears. This was one of the best things I have ever played. Now a days, I use a hardcore mod. Mods are available for Far Cry 3 that can fix things, or make the game more realistic and hard. Now, obviously Far Cry 3 being my favorite, I cannot wait for the release of Far Cry 4 which only comes in a couple weeks. I cannot WAIT.

[h1]Pro's & Con's (Overall Rating)[/h1]
Far Cry 3 is a great game that is well worth the time. For the story, the world, and the gameplay. Every piece of this game is full of greatness. You ability to do what you want beings a new level to video games. We need more, like this.

Pro's:
+Amazing story.
+Great memorable characters.
+Beautiful world that's full of life.
+Great weapon mechanics.
+Fantastic gameplay.
+Big populated open world.

Con's:
-Second half of game falls a little short.
-Some of the crafting is strange.
-Skill tree could use a little work.

Overall Rating: About a 14/15 (Must Own!)
